text.p: Estonian newspapers carried the following reports in their Tuesday editions. Reuters has not verified these reports and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
- Pentathlete Erki Nool returned from France after willing the silver medal in indoor World Championship.
- State court chairman Rait Maruste described the acquittal of a lawyer accused of bribery as shocking and said he hoped the prosecution would appeal.
- Russia supported Russian organisations in Estonia to the tune of 500 million roubles in 1995/96.
- Defence Force commander Colonel Johannes Kert received a badge of merit of the state of Maryland for efficient command of the Defence League and Defence Forces.
- Lauri Leesi, director of the Lycee Francais of Tallinn, will be awarded the order of Palmes Academiques from the French government for his efforts in promoting French culture in Estonia.
- Education Minister Rein Loik has announced he will resign and return to private business.
- U.S. Baltic organisations are to write to U.S. President Bill Clinton to argue that the Baltic countries should be admitted to NATO in the first round of enlargement.
- A border guard discovered an underground tube under the Latvian-Estonian border, believed to be used for smuggling vodka across the border. Vodka costs 60 percent more in Estonia.
- Prime Minister designate Mart Siimann will announce his programme on Wednesday, March 12, to appeal for parliament's approval to form a government.
- Banking specialists claim the Bank of Tallinn suffered a liquidity crisis early this year.
- The MRP private bus firm has promised to pay the wages due to drivers. Bus drivers threatened to strike last week.
- Estonian ski maker AS Viisnurk is to sign a deal with ski company Atomic on the sale of 70,000 pairs of skis.
